sections.section: Level 2 · Symbolism, the Nabis and Lautrec

tracks.title: A station that became a museum
tracks.where: Play this as you arrive, outside the building or just inside, before the galleries. Follow the museum's signs in; you don't need to stand anywhere in particular.
tracks.what: The Musée d'Orsay, built by Victor Laloux as the Gare d'Orsay, a railway station and hotel for the 1900 Exposition universelle, and opened as a museum in December 1986.
tracks.listen: How a station dressed up as a palace nearly gave way to a hotel, and how it became a museum instead.

tracks.room: Top of the central aisle · Level 0
tracks.title: The nave
tracks.where: At the top of the central aisle on level 0, looking down the length of the great hall towards the two towers at its far end.
tracks.what: The great hall of the former Gare d'Orsay, adapted by ACT-Architecture with interiors led by Gae Aulenti: a central sculpture aisle, side galleries on level 0, terraces on level 2, and the upper galleries on level 5.
tracks.listen: How the building works, floor by floor, and the route this walk takes through it.

tracks.title: Couture — Romains de la décadence
tracks.where: In the central sculpture aisle on level 0, in front of the huge canvas, nearly eight metres wide, of a Roman orgy in a classical hall watched by statues of the ancestors.
tracks.what: Thomas Couture, Romains de la décadence, Romans of the Decadence, 1847, oil on canvas, 472 × 772 cm. Commissioned by the State and shown at the Salon of 1847.
tracks.listen: A painting of ancient Rome that Paris read as a painting of itself.

tracks.title: Ingres — La Source
tracks.where: In room 1, the first room on the Lille side of level 0, in front of a tall, narrow canvas of a standing nude, set as if in an alcove.
tracks.what: Jean-Auguste-Dominique Ingres, La Source, The Spring, begun around 1820 in Florence and finished in Paris in 1856, oil on canvas, 163 × 80 cm.
tracks.listen: A painting that took thirty-six years and other people's hands, and the collector who staged it among real water plants.

tracks.title: Cabanel and Bouguereau — Two Venuses
tracks.where: In room 3 on the Lille side of level 0. Cabanel's Venus is the wide, low canvas, more than two metres across; Bouguereau's is the tall one, three metres high.
tracks.what: Alexandre Cabanel, Naissance de Vénus, The Birth of Venus, 1863, oil on canvas, 130 × 225 cm. William Bouguereau, Naissance de Vénus, The Birth of Venus, 1879, oil on canvas, 300 × 215 cm.
tracks.listen: Why the Second Empire loved painted goddesses, Zola's verdict on one of them, and what Manet did the same year.

tracks.title: Carpeaux — Ugolin
tracks.where: In the central sculpture aisle on level 0, at the bronze group of a father with his children, nearly two metres high.
tracks.what: Jean-Baptiste Carpeaux, Ugolin et ses enfants, Ugolino and his Children, bronze cast by Victor Thiébaut in 1863 from the plaster finished in Rome in 1861, 194 × 148 × 119 cm.
tracks.listen: A young sculptor who overstayed in Rome, argued with his elders, and turned a scene from Dante into bronze.

tracks.title: Daumier — The Célébrités du Juste Milieu
tracks.where: In room 4 on the Seine side of level 0, at the small painted clay busts of men of the July Monarchy. Some are barely the height of a hand; how many are on show may vary.
tracks.what: Honoré Daumier, Les Célébrités du Juste Milieu, Celebrities of the Juste Milieu, 1832–1835, busts in unbaked clay painted in oil. Thirty-six survive, all in this museum.
tracks.listen: Who ordered these caricature heads, why they survived, and the nicknames that went with them.

tracks.title: Millet — Des glaneuses (The Gleaners)
tracks.where: In room 5 on the Seine side of level 0, in front of a canvas about a metre wide of three women gleaning in a field, with the harvest behind them. From 14 November 2026 to 28 March 2027 it is on loan to Tokyo: if the wall is empty, listen in front of Millet's L'Angélus, in this room 5 or in Galerie Seine 1, the Alfred Chauchard collection gallery on the Seine side close by, instead.
tracks.what: Jean-François Millet, Des glaneuses, The Gleaners, 1857, oil on canvas, 83.5 × 110 cm. Shown at the Salon of 1857; given by Madame Pommery in 1890.
tracks.listen: What gleaning was, the ten years Millet spent on it, and why the harvest is pushed into the distance.

tracks.title: Millet — L'Angélus
tracks.where: In the Millet room, room 5, on the Seine side of level 0, or close by in Galerie Seine 1, the Alfred Chauchard collection gallery: Chauchard left the painting to the Louvre, and it may hang with the rest of his collection. Look for a small canvas, about 55 by 66 centimetres, of a man and a woman who have stopped work in a potato field, with a fork, a basket, sacks and a wheelbarrow.
tracks.what: Jean-François Millet, L'Angélus, The Angelus, 1857–1859, oil on canvas, 55.5 × 66 cm. Bequest of Alfred Chauchard.
tracks.listen: The grandmother behind the painting, and the strange fame that followed it.

tracks.title: Courbet — Un enterrement à Ornans (A Burial at Ornans)
tracks.where: In room 7 on the Seine side of level 0, in front of the enormous canvas, more than six metres wide, of a crowd of life-size villagers at a funeral. It is back on the wall after its restoration, finished in August 2026.
tracks.what: Gustave Courbet, Un enterrement à Ornans, A Burial at Ornans, 1849–1850, oil on canvas, 315 × 668 cm. Given by the artist's sister, Juliette Courbet, in 1881.
tracks.listen: An unknown funeral painted at the scale of history, the medal that let it past the jury, and what fifteen months of restoration brought back.

tracks.title: Courbet — L'Atelier du peintre (The Painter's Studio)
tracks.where: In room 7 on the Seine side of level 0, the same room as A Burial at Ornans, in front of the other huge canvas, about six metres wide: a crowded studio, with groups of figures on either side.
tracks.what: Gustave Courbet, L'Atelier du peintre. Allégorie réelle déterminant une phase de sept années de ma vie artistique, The Painter's Studio, 1854–1855, oil on canvas, 361 × 598 cm. Bought in 1920 by public subscription with the help of the Société des Amis du Louvre.
tracks.listen: Courbet's whole world in one room, a hunter who looks like the Emperor, a friend who hated his portrait, and a painting the public paid for twice.

tracks.title: Courbet — L'Origine du monde (optional)
tracks.where: Optional stop. In the Courbet rooms, 6 and 7, on the Seine side of level 0; the plan does not place this work, so look for a small canvas, about 46 by 55 centimetres, a very frank painting of the female body. If it is not on show, go on to room 14.
tracks.what: Gustave Courbet, L'Origine du monde, The Origin of the World, 1866, oil on canvas, 46.3 × 55.4 cm. Entered the museum in 1995 in lieu of inheritance tax.
tracks.listen: Who owned this painting, why it was so rarely seen, and who the model was.

tracks.title: Manet — Olympia
tracks.where: Room 14 on this floor, Seine side, the Manet room. Stand in front of the nude who looks straight out at you, with a black servant holding a bouquet at the centre and a black cat at the right.
tracks.what: Édouard Manet, Olympia, 1863, oil on canvas, 130.5 × 191 cm. Shown at the Salon of 1865; given to the State in 1890 by nearly a hundred subscribers led by Claude Monet.
tracks.listen: How a Salon scandal became a gift to the nation, who the two women really are, and the most famous cat in painting.

tracks.title: Manet — Le Fifre and Émile Zola
tracks.where: Room 14, the same room as Olympia. Le Fifre is the tall portrait of a boy from a military band against a plain background. Émile Zola shows the writer seated at his work table, with pictures on the wall behind him.
tracks.what: Édouard Manet, Le Fifre, The Fifer, 1866, oil on canvas, 160.5 × 97 cm, Camondo bequest 1911; and Émile Zola, 1868, oil on canvas, 146 × 114 cm, given by Madame Zola in 1918.
tracks.listen: A painting the Salon turned down, and the portrait Manet painted to thank the writer who defended him.

tracks.title: Fantin-Latour — Un atelier aux Batignolles
tracks.where: In Galerie Seine 2 on level 0, the gallery of portraits of the 1860s. A very large canvas, about two metres high and nearly three wide, of eight men gathered in a studio, one of them a painter at his easel.
tracks.what: Henri Fantin-Latour, Un atelier aux Batignolles, A Studio at Les Batignolles, 1870, oil on canvas, 204 × 273.5 cm. Shown at the Salon of 1870; bought in 1892.
tracks.listen: Who the eight men are, why they gather around Manet, and the least famous of them.

tracks.title: Manet — Le Déjeuner sur l'herbe
tracks.where: Room 18 on this floor, where the museum lists it. If the painting is not there, it may have moved to room 29 on level 5, the Moreau-Nélaton collection room: listen wherever you find it. It is the large picnic painting, about two metres high and two and a half metres wide.
tracks.what: Édouard Manet, Le Déjeuner sur l'herbe, Luncheon on the Grass, 1863, oil on canvas, 207 × 265 cm. Given to the national museums by Étienne Moreau-Nélaton in 1906.
tracks.listen: The Emperor's show for rejected paintings, the old masters hidden in this modern picnic, and the painter it provoked.

tracks.title: Monet — Femmes au jardin
tracks.where: Room 18, the same room as Manet's Déjeuner sur l'herbe. A tall canvas, about two and a half metres high, of women in a garden.
tracks.what: Claude Monet, Femmes au jardin, Women in the Garden, around 1866, oil on canvas, 255 × 205 cm. Bought from Monet by the State in 1921.
tracks.listen: The trench and pulley Monet needed to paint it, the one model behind three women, and the whites a recent cleaning brought back.

tracks.title: Bazille — L'Atelier de Bazille
tracks.where: Room 18 on level 0, the room of Bazille, Monet and Renoir in the 1860s, the same room as Monet's Femmes au jardin. Look for a painting of a studio interior with several men in it: a tall, slim painter holding a palette stands in the middle, and a man in a hat looks at the canvas on the easel.
tracks.what: Frédéric Bazille, L'Atelier de Bazille, Bazille's Studio, 1870, oil on canvas, 98 × 128 cm. Bequeathed by the artist's brother, Marc Bazille, in 1924.
tracks.listen: The studio Bazille shared with Renoir, and the friend who painted Bazille into his own picture.

tracks.title: Who do these works belong to? The MNR room
tracks.where: Room 10b, on the Lille side of level 0 at the far end of the nave, under the title « À qui appartiennent ces œuvres ? ». The selection of about thirteen works changes over time, and some paintings are hung so that you can see their backs.
tracks.what: A room opened in May 2026 for works in the MNR category, recovered after the Second World War and held by the national museums until their owners can be identified.
tracks.listen: What MNR means, why so few works have gone home, and what the backs of these paintings can tell.

tracks.title: Cézanne — Le Christ aux limbes and Une moderne Olympia
tracks.where: In room 11 on level 0, the room of Cézanne's beginnings. Le Christ aux limbes is the tall painting, about 1.7 metres high, of Christ going down among waiting figures. Une moderne Olympia is the small, bright canvas of a naked woman, a servant and a watching man in black.
tracks.what: Paul Cézanne, Le Christ aux limbes, Christ in Limbo, about 1869, oil on plaster transferred to canvas, 168.5 × 100.5 cm. Une moderne Olympia, A Modern Olympia, 1873–1874, oil on canvas, 46.2 × 55.5 cm, gift of Paul Gachet, 1951.
tracks.listen: A mural cut off a family wall and refused by the State, and Cézanne's cheeky reply to Manet's Olympia.

tracks.title: Degas — La Famille Bellelli (The Bellelli Family)
tracks.where: In room 13 on level 0, the Degas room, in front of the very large family portrait, about two by two and a half metres: a mother in mourning with two girls, the father turned away. Its room is not confirmed and from 14 November 2026 to 28 March 2027 it may be on loan to Tokyo: if you can't find it, listen in front of Sémiramis construisant Babylone, the wide canvas of a queen on a riverbank watching a city rise, in this room.
tracks.what: Edgar Degas, Portrait de famille, also called La Famille Bellelli, The Bellelli Family, 1858–1869, oil on canvas, 201 × 249.5 cm, RF 2210. Bought at the first Degas studio sale in 1918. Stand-in: Sémiramis construisant Babylone, begun about 1860, oil on canvas, 151.5 × 258 cm.
tracks.listen: A grandfather watching from the wall, a family split down the middle, and a young Degas who wanted to paint history.

tracks.title: Carpeaux — La Danse
tracks.where: In the central sculpture aisle on level 0. The large stone group, over four metres high, of six dancing women in a ring around the Genius of Dance, with a small putto.
tracks.what: Jean-Baptiste Carpeaux, La Danse, The Dance, 1869, Échaillon stone, 420 × 298 × 145 cm, about 18 tonnes. The original group from the façade of the Paris Opéra.
tracks.listen: An ink attack, a sculpture saved by a war, and why the group on the Opéra today is a copy.

tracks.room: End of the nave · Opéra space · Level 0
tracks.title: The Opéra quarter in 1914
tracks.where: In the Opéra space at the end of the nave, level 0: a model of the streets around the Opéra, six and a half metres square, seen from above beneath a transparent floor. From October 2026 to mid-January 2027 a temporary display is built around these models, so access or presentation may differ; follow the museum's signs.
tracks.what: Rémi Munier, with Eric de Leusse, Jean-Luc Bethmont and Borani Hoy, Maquette du quartier de l'Opéra, arrêtée en l'état en 1914, model of the Opéra quarter as it stood in 1914, 1984–86, resin under plexiglass, 650 × 650 cm.
tracks.listen: A whole quarter of Paris stopped in one year, and why the museum built it.

tracks.room: End of the nave · Opéra space · Level 0
tracks.title: Garnier's Opéra, cut open
tracks.where: In the Opéra space at the end of the nave, level 0: a long model of the Paris Opéra sliced lengthwise, nearly six metres long and about two and a half metres high. In autumn 2026 a temporary display is built around the models, so access may differ; follow the museum's signs.
tracks.what: Opéra de Paris, maquette de la coupe longitudinale, longitudinal-section model of the Paris Opéra, made in 1985 in Rome by the Gianese workshop under Richard Peduzzi's artistic direction, after Garnier's own drawing, at 1/25 scale, 240 × 578 × 110 cm.
tracks.listen: How to read an opera house from the façade to the back of the stage, and why the model was made.

tracks.room: Paris rooms · far end of the nave · Level 0
tracks.title: Paris, capital of a modern nation
tracks.where: In the rooms at the far end of the nave on level 0 called « Paris, capitale d'une nation moderne », by the escalators to level 5. Look for Victor Navlet's large painted view of the whole city seen from above.
tracks.what: Rooms opened in May 2022 on the transformation of Paris under the Second Empire, centred on Victor Navlet's Vue générale de Paris, prise de l'Observatoire en ballon, General View of Paris from the Observatory in a Balloon, 1855, and on Garnier's Opéra.
tracks.listen: What these rooms set out to show, and a bird's-eye view of Paris from a balloon.

tracks.room: End of the nave · between the towers · Level 0
tracks.title: Rodin — The Gates of Hell
tracks.where: At the far end of the nave, between the two towers, on the axis of the central aisle: Rodin's great plaster doorway, more than six metres high. Afterwards, go back to the escalators by the Paris rooms and ride up to level 5, to the clock salon.
tracks.what: Auguste Rodin, La Porte de l'Enfer, The Gates of Hell, the original plaster, 6.35 m high, worked on from 1880 to 1917.
tracks.listen: A door made for a museum that was never built, the decades Rodin spent on it, and why it was standing in front of you from the moment you came in.

tracks.title: The clock over Paris
tracks.where: Room 28, the Salon de l'horloge, at the top of the escalators on level 5, before the Impressionist rooms: stand in the alcove behind the great clock face set into the façade, looking out through the dial towards the Seine.
tracks.what: One of the great illuminated clocks of the former Gare d'Orsay, the station built for the 1900 Exposition universelle, kept on purpose when the station became a museum.
tracks.listen: Why a museum kept its station clocks, and what it means to stand behind one.

tracks.title: Monet — the Déjeuner sur l'herbe fragments
tracks.where: Room 29, level 5. Two very large canvases from one picnic scene, hung side by side: the big central fragment, almost two and a half metres tall, and the left-hand fragment hung to its left.
tracks.what: Claude Monet, Le Déjeuner sur l'herbe, Luncheon on the Grass, begun 1865, oil on canvas: two surviving fragments, the central one 248.7 × 218 cm.
tracks.listen: How the biggest canvas of Monet's youth ended up as rent security, then mouldy, then in pieces.

tracks.title: Monet — Coquelicots
tracks.where: Room 29, level 5. A small landscape of a field of red poppies, with a woman holding a sunshade and a child in the foreground.
tracks.what: Claude Monet, Coquelicots, Poppies, 1873, oil on canvas, 50 × 65.3 cm. Painted at Argenteuil. Gift of Étienne Moreau-Nélaton, 1906.
tracks.listen: The exhibition of 1874, the family in the poppies, and the collector who gave this picture and Manet's picnic to the nation in the same year.

tracks.title: Pissarro — Gelée blanche
tracks.where: In the Impressionist rooms on level 5; the exact room is not confirmed. Look for a wide landscape of frosted, furrowed fields, with a man carrying dead wood along a path, signed and dated lower left.
tracks.what: Camille Pissarro, Gelée blanche, Hoarfrost, 1873, oil on canvas, 65.5 × 93.2 cm, painted at Pontoise. Shown at the first Impressionist exhibition in 1874.
tracks.listen: What a famous critic said about this frost, word for word, and why it says more about him than about the painting.

tracks.title: Monet — La Gare Saint-Lazare
tracks.where: Room 31, level 5. Monet's painting of the inside of a Paris railway station, the hall filled with steam and light.
tracks.what: Claude Monet, La Gare Saint-Lazare, The Saint-Lazare Station, 1877, oil on canvas, 75 × 105 cm. Caillebotte bequest, accepted by the State in 1896.
tracks.listen: How Monet found a subject on the edge of his new neighbourhood, and how a painter friend paid 685 francs for it and ended up giving it to France.

tracks.title: Caillebotte — Raboteurs de parquet
tracks.where: Room 31, level 5, the same room as Monet's Gare Saint-Lazare. A large canvas of workmen scraping the boards of a bare floor.
tracks.what: Gustave Caillebotte, Raboteurs de parquet, The Floor Scrapers, 1875, oil on canvas, 102 × 147 cm. Given by the Caillebotte heirs through Auguste Renoir, 1894.
tracks.listen: Why the Salon jury rejected a painting of men at work, and how it reached the nation by a side door.

tracks.title: Degas — La Classe de danse
tracks.where: Room 31, level 5, the same room as Monet's Gare Saint-Lazare and Caillebotte's Floor Scrapers. A ballet class in a rehearsal room, the ballet master among his young pupils.
tracks.what: Edgar Degas, La Classe de danse, The Dance Class, 1873–1876, oil on canvas, 85.5 × 75 cm. Bequest of Count Isaac de Camondo, 1911.
tracks.listen: A real ballet master in a class that never happened, in an opera house that had already burned down.

tracks.title: Degas — Petite danseuse de quatorze ans
tracks.where: Room 32, level 5. A free-standing figure of a young dancer, just under a metre tall, in dark patinated bronze with a real tulle tutu and a satin ribbon, on a wooden base. You can walk around her.
tracks.what: Edgar Degas, Petite danseuse de quatorze ans, Little Dancer Aged Fourteen: a posthumous bronze, cast by the lost-wax method by the founder Adrien-Aurélien Hébrard between 1921 and 1931, after Degas's wax model of 1878–1881. Patinated bronze, tulle, satin, wood. Height 98 cm. Acquired in 1931.
tracks.listen: Who the girl was, what Paris saw in 1881, and why the figure in front of you is a faithful copy made after Degas died.

tracks.title: Morisot — Le Berceau
tracks.where: Room 32, level 5, the same room as Degas's Little Dancer. A smallish painting of a young woman watching over a baby asleep in a cradle.
tracks.what: Berthe Morisot, Le Berceau, The Cradle, 1872, oil on canvas, 56 × 46.5 cm. Bought by the Louvre in 1930.
tracks.listen: The first woman to show with the Impressionists, her sister and niece, and the baby who grew up and sold this picture to the nation.

tracks.title: Degas — L'Absinthe
tracks.where: In the Impressionist rooms on level 5; the exact room is not confirmed. Look for a man and a woman sitting side by side on a café banquette, a marble table in front of them and a glass of absinthe before her, the picture framed well off-centre.
tracks.what: Edgar Degas, Dans un café, In a Café, also called L'Absinthe, 1875–1876, oil on canvas, 92 × 68.5 cm. Bequest of Count Isaac de Camondo, 1911.
tracks.listen: Two friends cast as strangers, a real Paris café, and the odd framing that makes the whole picture feel unsteady.

tracks.title: Renoir — Bal du moulin de la Galette
tracks.where: In the Impressionist rooms on level 5; the room is not confirmed, so look for Renoir's large canvas of a crowded Parisian dance, couples dancing and friends talking around a table.
tracks.what: Pierre-Auguste Renoir, Bal du moulin de la Galette, Dance at the Moulin de la Galette, 1876, oil on canvas, about 131 × 175 cm. Caillebotte bequest, accepted 1896.
tracks.listen: Who the dancers really were, the young model called Margot, and the painter-collector who left it to the nation.

tracks.title: Sisley — La Barque pendant l'inondation, Port-Marly
tracks.where: In the Impressionist rooms on level 5; the room is not confirmed. Look for a small flood scene: a house with pink and yellow walls standing at an angle, wide sky above and floodwater all around.
tracks.what: Alfred Sisley, La Barque pendant l'inondation, Port-Marly, The Boat in the Flood, 1876, oil on canvas, 50.4 × 61 cm. Bequest of comte Isaac de Camondo, 1911.
tracks.listen: The first owner whose household later joined Monet's, the spring the Seine came into town, and the six pictures Sisley made of it.

tracks.title: Monet — The Rouen Cathedrals
tracks.where: In room 34 on level 5, in front of Monet's five paintings of the doorway and front of Rouen Cathedral, hung together.
tracks.what: Claude Monet, five canvases from the series La Cathédrale de Rouen, Rouen Cathedral, painted 1892–93, oil on canvas: Le Portail, soleil matinal; Le Portail et la tour Saint-Romain, effet du matin; Le Portail et la tour Saint-Romain, plein soleil; Le Portail, temps gris; Le Portail vu de face. Four from the Camondo bequest of 1911, one bought from Monet in 1907.
tracks.listen: Monet's nightmare about the cathedral, the thirty canvases of one stone front, and how to read the five that hang here.

tracks.title: Monet — Nymphéas bleus (Blue Water Lilies)
tracks.where: In room 34 on level 5, the same room as the Rouen Cathedrals. Look for a large, square canvas of water lilies, about two metres each way.
tracks.what: Claude Monet, Nymphéas bleus, Blue Water Lilies, around 1916–1919, oil on canvas, 204 × 200 cm.
tracks.listen: The pond Monet made in the same years as the cathedrals, and why this picture seems to have no edges.

tracks.title: Cézanne — Les Joueurs de cartes (The Card Players)
tracks.where: In the Cézanne rooms on level 5; the room is not confirmed. Look for a small painting of men playing cards at a table, one of them smoking a pipe.
tracks.what: Paul Cézanne, Les Joueurs de cartes, The Card Players, 1893–1896, oil on canvas, 47 × 56.5 cm. The smallest of five versions. Bequest of comte Isaac de Camondo, 1911.
tracks.listen: Who the card players may have been, the gardener with the pipe, and why the smallest version of a famous subject holds its own.

tracks.title: Cézanne — Pommes et oranges (Apples and Oranges)
tracks.where: In the Cézanne rooms on level 5; the room is not confirmed. Look for a large still life of apples and oranges on dishes, with draped cloth and a flower-patterned jug. Orsay also owns views of the Montagne Sainte-Victoire, which may or may not be hanging nearby.
tracks.what: Paul Cézanne, Pommes et oranges, Apples and Oranges, around 1899, oil on canvas, 74 × 93 cm. Bequest of comte Isaac de Camondo, 1911.
tracks.listen: Six paintings from the same props, and why the museum calls this the most important still life of his late years.

tracks.title: Van Gogh in France
tracks.where: At the entrance to room 36 on level 5, the Van Gogh room, at the end of the Impressionist gallery. You'll know it by the picture rails, painted blue.
tracks.what: The Van Gogh room, rehung in February 2024. Room 36, Vincent van Gogh in France, follows him from Paris to Arles, Saint-Rémy and Auvers-sur-Oise, and his bond with Dr Paul Gachet.
tracks.listen: How this room is laid out, the journey it follows, and the last two months that fill the final walls.

tracks.title: Van Gogh — Portrait de l'artiste (Self-Portrait), 1889
tracks.where: In room 36 on level 5, in front of Van Gogh's head-and-shoulders self-portrait in a suit, against a swirling background of pale green and turquoise, with bright orange hair and beard.
tracks.what: Vincent van Gogh, Portrait de l'artiste, Self-Portrait, 1889, painted at Saint-Rémy-de-Provence, oil on canvas, 65 × 54.2 cm. Gift of Paul and Marguerite Gachet, 1949.
tracks.listen: The doctor's family who kept this portrait for decades, what Van Gogh wrote about painting himself, and the stillness at the centre of a moving picture.

tracks.title: Van Gogh — La Chambre de Van Gogh à Arles (Van Gogh's Bedroom in Arles)
tracks.where: In the Van Gogh rooms on level 5; the exact room is not confirmed. Look for a small painting of a simple bedroom with a yellow bed and chairs, a red floor and pale lilac walls.
tracks.what: Vincent van Gogh, La Chambre de Van Gogh à Arles, Van Gogh's Bedroom in Arles, 1889, oil on canvas, 57.3 × 73.5 cm, RF 1959 2. A smaller version painted about a year after the 1888 original. A larger version is in the Art Institute of Chicago.
tracks.listen: A painting meant to rest the mind, made smaller for his family, and the post-war treaty that brought it into the French collection.

tracks.title: Van Gogh — La Nuit étoilée (Starry Night over the Rhône)
tracks.where: In room 36 on level 5, in front of Van Gogh's night view of the Rhône: deep blue sky and water, bright stars, and the orange gaslights of Arles reflected in the river. Note: it is on loan to Tokyo from 14 November 2026 to 28 March 2027; if the wall is empty, listen in front of the 1889 self-portrait in a suit, which hangs in the same room.
tracks.what: Vincent van Gogh, La Nuit étoilée, Starry Night over the Rhône, 1888, Arles, oil on canvas, 73 × 92 cm. Gift of M. and Mme Robert Kahn-Sriber in memory of M. and Mme Fernand Moch, 1975.
tracks.listen: A painting made outdoors at night by gaslight, the colours Van Gogh saw in the dark, the lovers at the bottom, and a last look at the self-portrait nearby.

tracks.title: Van Gogh — L'Église d'Auvers-sur-Oise (The Church at Auvers)
tracks.where: In room 36 on level 5, in front of Van Gogh's painting of the village church at Auvers, seen from its apse end, its windows in deep blue patches under a cobalt sky.
tracks.what: Vincent van Gogh, L'Église d'Auvers-sur-Oise, vue du chevet, The Church at Auvers-sur-Oise, seen from the apse, painted 4–8 June 1890, oil on canvas, 93 × 74.5 cm. Acquired in 1952 with the support of Paul Gachet and an anonymous Canadian donation.
tracks.listen: What Van Gogh himself wrote about this church, the colour of its windows, and the stranger who helped bring it to the museum.

tracks.title: Van Gogh — Le Docteur Paul Gachet
tracks.where: In room 36 on level 5, the Van Gogh room. Look for Van Gogh's portrait of a melancholy man painted in cold colours, with a sprig of foxglove.
tracks.what: Vincent van Gogh, Portrait du Docteur Gachet, Dr Paul Gachet, 1890, oil on canvas, 68 × 57 cm, RF 1949 16. Part of the gift of the Gachet heirs, 1949–1954.
tracks.listen: Who Dr Gachet was, the false name he painted under, and the one hopeful thing Van Gogh put in his portrait.

tracks.title: Seurat — Le Cirque
tracks.where: Room 38 on level 5, the Seurat and Neo-Impressionist room. Look for a large, tall canvas of a circus ring made of tiny touches of colour, with a clown seen from behind in the foreground and a painted blue border.
tracks.what: Georges Seurat, Le Cirque (Circus), 1890–91, left unfinished. Oil on canvas, 186 × 152 cm. Bequest of John Quinn, accepted by the State in 1927.
tracks.listen: The painting Seurat showed days before he died, the theory that makes everything in it climb, and the frame that belongs to the picture.

tracks.title: Signac — Femme à l'ombrelle
tracks.where: Room 40 on level 5, among the Neo-Impressionists. Look for Paul Signac's portrait of a woman with a parasol, painted in small separate touches of colour. More Signac hangs in room 39.
tracks.what: Paul Signac, Femme à l'ombrelle (Woman with a Parasol), 1893. Oil on canvas, 81 × 65 cm.
tracks.listen: The woman Signac met at a cabaret and painted after ten years together, and how the next generation took the Impressionists' favourite subject and remade it in dots.

tracks.title: Émile Bernard — Madeleine au Bois d'Amour
tracks.where: In room 43 on level 5, the Pont-Aven room. Look for a large, wide canvas with a life-size young woman lying full length in a wood.
tracks.what: Émile Bernard, Madeleine au Bois d'Amour (Madeleine in the Bois d'Amour), 1888. Oil on canvas, 137 × 163 cm. Acquired in 1977.
tracks.listen: A brother of twenty paints his sister of seventeen, and the older painter who was in love with her.

tracks.title: Gauguin — La Belle Angèle and Les Alyscamps
tracks.where: In room 43 on level 5, the Pont-Aven room. La Belle Angèle is a woman's portrait set inside a circle on a decorative background, with a strange pot beside her. Les Alyscamps is a landscape in bright autumn colours with three small walkers; it may hang nearby.
tracks.what: Paul Gauguin, La Belle Angèle (The Beautiful Angèle), 1889, oil on canvas, 92 × 73.2 cm, gift of Ambroise Vollard, 1927. Paul Gauguin, Les Alyscamps, 1888, oil on canvas, 91.5 × 72.5 cm.
tracks.listen: A portrait its sitter refused and Degas bought, and a landscape Gauguin gave a mocking title.

tracks.title: Gauguin — Arearea
tracks.where: In room 44 on level 5, Gauguin in Tahiti. Look for a Tahitian scene with two women seated at the centre, a tree cutting across the picture and a red dog in the foreground. On loan to Tokyo from 14 Nov 2026 to 28 Mar 2027 (it may leave the wall earlier): then use Femmes de Tahiti, if it is on display.
tracks.what: Paul Gauguin, Arearea (Joyeusetés), 1892. Oil on canvas, 75 × 94 cm. Bequest of M. and Mme Lung, 1961. Fallback: Paul Gauguin, Femmes de Tahiti (Tahitian Women), 1891, oil on canvas, 69 × 91.5 cm.
tracks.listen: The red dog Paris laughed at, the idol Gauguin invented, and why he bought this painting back. If it is away, the track works in front of Femmes de Tahiti.

tracks.title: Gauguin — Le Cheval blanc (The White Horse)
tracks.where: On level 5 in the Galerie Françoise Cachin, in the Gauguin in Tahiti room, room 44 on the plan, in front of an upright canvas about 1.4 metres high: a pale horse drinking from a stream, with two riders behind it. The room number is inferred from the plan; check nearby if needed.
tracks.what: Paul Gauguin, Le Cheval blanc, The White Horse, 1898, oil on canvas, 140.5 × 92 cm, RF 2616. Painted during his second stay in Tahiti. From the collection of Daniel de Monfreid, acquired 1927.
tracks.listen: A commission turned down over the colour of a horse, and a Tahiti that Gauguin made up.

tracks.title: Gauguin — Oviri
tracks.where: On level 5 in the Galerie Françoise Cachin, near the Gauguin paintings of room 44: a standing stoneware figure, about 75 centimetres high, over a dead wolf and a cub. Its exact place in the gallery is not confirmed; check nearby.
tracks.what: Paul Gauguin, Oviri, 1894, partially glazed stoneware, 75 × 19 × 27 cm, about 20 kg, OAO 1114. Fired in Ernest Chaplet's kiln in December 1894. Acquired 1987.
tracks.listen: The biggest ceramic Gauguin ever made, the name he gave it, and where he wanted it to end up.

tracks.title: Henri Rousseau — La Charmeuse de serpents (The Snake Charmer)
tracks.where: On level 5 in the Galerie Françoise Cachin, near the Gauguin rooms: a large, nearly square jungle scene, almost 1.9 metres wide, with a dark figure playing a flute and snakes around it. Its room is not confirmed. It was on loan until July 2026; if it is not on show, skip this track and go on to room 45.
tracks.what: Henri Rousseau, La Charmeuse de serpents, The Snake Charmer, 1907, oil on canvas, 169 × 189.5 cm. Bequest of Jacques Doucet, 1936.
tracks.listen: A jungle painted without leaving Paris, the woman who ordered it, and the artists it went on to haunt.

tracks.room: Room 45 · Redon and the Nabis · Level 5
tracks.title: Sérusier — Le Talisman
tracks.where: In room 45 on level 5, Redon and the Nabis, after the Gauguin rooms. Look for a very small landscape painted on a wooden panel, about the size of a sheet of paper.
tracks.what: Paul Sérusier, Le Talisman (L'Aven au Bois d'Amour), October 1888. Oil on wood, 27 × 21 cm.
tracks.listen: How a panel smaller than a sheet of paper, painted under Gauguin's direction, became the founding work of the Nabis.

tracks.room: Room 45 · Redon and the Nabis · Level 5
tracks.title: Odilon Redon — Les Yeux clos (Closed Eyes)
tracks.where: In room 45 on level 5, Redon and the Nabis, in the Galerie Françoise Cachin: a small painting, 44 × 36 cm, of a head and shoulders with closed eyes, floating in a soft, undefined space. The room number is inferred from the plan; check nearby if needed.
tracks.what: Odilon Redon, Les Yeux clos, Closed Eyes, 1890, oil, 44 × 36 cm, signed and dated. Chosen from the artist's studio in 1904 by Léonce Bénédite for the Musée du Luxembourg.
tracks.listen: A face turned inwards, the first Redon the State ever took, and his farewell to Gauguin.

tracks.room: Room 46 · Le cabaret du Chat noir · Level 5
tracks.title: Le cabaret du Chat noir — the shadow theatre
tracks.where: In room 46 on level 5, Le cabaret du Chat noir, after the Redon and Nabis room. Look for the flat silhouettes cut from zinc, once used in the cabaret's shadow theatre. Which figures are on show changes; check on site.
tracks.what: Cut and painted zinc silhouettes from the shadow theatre of the Cabaret du Chat Noir, Paris, 1886–1896, made under Henri Rivière.
tracks.listen: A Montmartre cabaret run by a showman, and a shadow theatre that looked forward to the cinema.

tracks.title: The birth of cinema, 1895–1914
tracks.where: In room 47 on level 5, Cinéma 1895–1914, next to the Chat Noir room. Early films play on three screens, with sound that reaches you only when you stand in front of each one. Display cases may hold optical toys and early photographs; what is on show changes, so check on site.
tracks.what: A room on the birth of the cinematograph: about fifteen films or excerpts from 1895 to 1914 on three screens, shown with directional "sound showers", alongside the optical devices and photographs that came before film.
tracks.listen: Why a museum of the nineteenth century ends with moving pictures, and the toys that taught the eye to see motion.

tracks.title: Behind the great clock
tracks.where: Beside the second great clock of the façade on level 5, by rooms 38 and 39, at the entrance to the Café Campana. Listen from the threshold; no need to go in.
tracks.what: The Café Campana, opened in 2011 with the renovated Impressionist gallery and designed by the Brazilian designers the Campana brothers, set behind one of the station's great exterior clocks.
tracks.listen: The underwater café behind the second great clock, a moment to sit down, and the way down to level two.

tracks.section: Level 2 · Symbolism, the Nabis and Lautrec
tracks.title: The Salle des fêtes — the hotel ballroom
tracks.where: In room 51 on level 2, the Salle des fêtes. Stand in the middle of the room with its mirrors and chandeliers, and look up at the painted panels high on the walls.
tracks.what: The ballroom of the former station hotel, opened with the Gare d'Orsay on 14 July 1900, restored rather than reconstructed. Painted décor by Pierre Fritel, 1900, oil on canvas fixed to plaster, commissioned by the Compagnie des chemins de fer d'Orléans.
tracks.listen: A ballroom built for railway travellers, the one period room the museum kept, and a famous press conference in 1958.

tracks.section: Level 2 · Symbolism, the Nabis and Lautrec
tracks.title: Gustave Moreau — Orphée
tracks.where: Room 59 on level 2, the Symbolism room at the west end of the floor; the painting's own page gives room 57, so look next door if it is not here. Look for an upright painting on wood of a girl in rich Oriental dress, holding a man's head that rests on a lyre, in front of a twilight landscape.
tracks.what: Gustave Moreau, Orphée, Orpheus, 1865, oil on wood, 154 × 99.5 cm. Shown at the Salon of 1866 and bought from the artist by the State.
tracks.listen: Why a severed head in Moreau's painting feels calm rather than horrifying, and the two faces that look alike.

tracks.section: Level 2 · Symbolism, the Nabis and Lautrec
tracks.title: Camille Claudel — L'Âge mûr
tracks.where: Room 55 on level 2, the history painting room at the west end of the floor. Look for a bronze group of three figures on a long base: an older man drawn away by an older woman, and a young woman on her knees, reaching after him.
tracks.what: Camille Claudel, L'Âge mûr, Maturity, about 1902, bronze group in three parts, 114 × 163 × 72 cm. The first bronze, cast in the artist's lifetime; at Orsay since 1982.
tracks.listen: The private patron who paid for the bronze the State never ordered, and why Claudel's brother saw her soul being torn away in it.

tracks.section: Level 2 · Symbolism, the Nabis and Lautrec
tracks.title: Vuillard — Jardins publics
tracks.where: Room 72 on level 2, the room with five large garden panels in beige, green and blue hung around a corner. Bonnard's tall, narrow panel of a woman in a cape hangs in the same room.
tracks.what: Édouard Vuillard, Jardins publics, Public Gardens, 1894, distemper on canvas: five panels of a cycle of nine. Also Pierre Bonnard, Femmes au jardin, Women in the Garden: Femme à la pèlerine, 1891, distemper on canvas.
tracks.listen: Standing in the corner of a dining room that no longer exists, and the painter his friends called the very Japanese Nabi.

tracks.section: Level 2 · Symbolism, the Nabis and Lautrec
tracks.title: Vallotton — Le Ballon
tracks.where: Room 71 on level 2. Look for a small, wide painting of a park seen from above: a broad stretch of ochre ground, dark trees, and a child in a yellow hat chasing a red ball.
tracks.what: Félix Vallotton, Le Ballon, The Ball, 1899, oil on cardboard mounted on wood, 49.2 × 62 cm. Carle Dreyfus bequest, 1953.
tracks.listen: How one small running child and a red ball can hold a whole empty park together.

tracks.section: Level 2 · Symbolism, the Nabis and Lautrec
tracks.title: Maurice Denis — Les Muses
tracks.where: Room 70 on level 2, in front of a tall canvas of women in the dress of the 1890s, gathered among the straight trunks of great chestnut trees.
tracks.what: Maurice Denis, Les Muses, The Muses, 1893, oil on canvas, 171 × 137.5 cm. Bought at public sale in 1932.
tracks.listen: How Denis turned the Muses of myth into women of his own day, and put his new wife among them.

tracks.section: Level 2 · Symbolism, the Nabis and Lautrec
tracks.title: Toulouse-Lautrec — Jane Avril dansant
tracks.where: Room 68 on level 2, the Toulouse-Lautrec room, « spectacles et coulisses ». It is a tall, narrow picture on cardboard of a woman dancing alone, painted in thin, quick strokes, with two figures behind her.
tracks.what: Henri de Toulouse-Lautrec, Jane Avril dansant (Jane Avril Dancing), around 1892. Oil on cardboard, 85.5 × 45 cm. Bequest of Antonin Personnaz, 1937.
tracks.listen: How a girl in a hospital for nervous illness discovered she could dance, and how Lautrec caught her in a few thin strokes.

tracks.section: Level 2 · Symbolism, the Nabis and Lautrec
tracks.title: Toulouse-Lautrec — La Clownesse Cha-U-Kao and La Goulue
tracks.where: Room 68 on level 2, the Toulouse-Lautrec room. Cha-U-Kao is a small picture on cardboard of a woman clown in a private room, fastening a large yellow ruffle, with green walls and a red sofa. La Goulue's two monumental booth panels may not be shown in this room.
tracks.what: Henri de Toulouse-Lautrec, La Clownesse Cha-U-Kao (The Clown Cha-U-Kao), 1895, oil on cardboard, 58 × 43 cm, Isaac de Camondo bequest, 1911. Panneaux pour la baraque de la Goulue, à la Foire du Trône à Paris (Panels for La Goulue's Booth at the Foire du Trône), 1895, oil.
tracks.listen: A clown whose stage name is a pun, a stranger in a mirror, and two fairground panels that were cut up and pieced back together.

tracks.title: Rodin — Balzac
tracks.where: On the Terrasse Rodin at the east end of level 2, by room 67, overlooking the nave: Rodin's towering plaster figure of the writer Balzac, almost three metres high.
tracks.what: Auguste Rodin, Balzac, 1898, plaster, 285 × 125 × 132 cm. Shown at the 1898 Salon of the Société nationale des beaux-arts.
tracks.listen: The monument Paris laughed at, why Rodin refused to sell it, and a dressing gown dipped in plaster.

tracks.title: Guimard and Majorelle — Art Nouveau
tracks.where: Room 64 on level 2, among the Art Nouveau furniture. Look for Guimard's tall wooden smoking-room bench with a leg like a branching tree trunk, and Majorelle's Water Lilies bed with its gilt bronze.
tracks.what: Hector Guimard, smoking-room bench, 1897, jarrah wood and carved metal, 260 × 262 cm. Louis Majorelle, Nénuphars bed, 1905–09, mahogany, amourette, marquetry and gilt bronze.
tracks.listen: The man behind the Paris Métro entrances, a bench that grows like a tree, and a bed in bloom.

tracks.title: Gallé and Carabin's bookcase
tracks.where: Rooms 63 and 65 on level 2. In room 63, a glass hand rising among shells and seaweed. In room 65, a walnut and wrought-iron bookcase almost three metres high, covered in carved figures.
tracks.what: Émile Gallé, La Main aux algues et aux coquillages, Hand with Seaweed and Shells, 1904, crystal with inclusions, applications and wheel engraving, 33.4 cm high. François-Rupert Carabin, Bibliothèque, Bookcase, 1890, walnut and wrought iron, 290 × 215 × 83 cm.
tracks.listen: A glassmaker's farewell piece, and a bookcase that preaches a sermon.

tracks.title: Pompon — Ours blanc
tracks.where: On the level-2 sculpture terrace overlooking the nave. Look for a large stone polar bear, about two and a half metres long.
tracks.what: François Pompon, Ours blanc, Polar Bear, stone, 163 × 251 × 90 cm, carved 1923–33 after a State commission of 1927. Assigned to Orsay in 1986.
tracks.listen: The man who carved marble for Rodin and Claudel, and found fame at sixty-seven with a bear.

tracks.title: Maillol and Bourdelle — Méditerranée and Héraklès archer
tracks.where: On the level-2 sculpture terrace overlooking the nave. Look for Maillol's seated woman in marble, and Bourdelle's large gilded bronze of Hercules drawing a bow.
tracks.what: Aristide Maillol, Méditerranée, The Mediterranean, 1923–27, marble, 110.5 × 117.5 × 68.5 cm. Antoine Bourdelle, Héraklès tue les oiseaux du lac Stymphale, Hercules the Archer, 1909, gilded bronze cast by Alexis Rudier, 248 × 247 × 123 cm.
tracks.listen: A woman with no name and no story, set against a hero a split second from letting go.

tracks.title: Out into Paris
tracks.where: On the level-2 sculpture terrace, at the balustrade, looking down the length of the nave towards Rodin's Gates of Hell at the far end.
tracks.what: The nave of the former Gare d'Orsay, seen from the sculpture terraces of level 2: built as a station for the 1900 Exposition, opened as a museum in December 1986.
tracks.listen: One last look down the old station, a short look back over the tour, and the way out.
